claims.text: Adding approximately 3 wt% Al to CoCrFeNi will promote formation of a continuous, self-adaptive alpha-Al2O3 tribolayer during sliding from room temperature to 800 °C.
The Al-modified alloy will have lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
The Al-modified alloy will have lower wear than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
Optimization of Al content or addition of a catalytic element may be required for effective low-temperature tribolayer formation.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a coarse-grained microstructure and lacks an intrinsic protective oxide layer.
The proposed primary intervention is addition of approximately 3 wt% Al to CoCrFeNi.
Sliding is to be evaluated in dry ambient air from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under about 50 N normal load.
The proposed tribolayer will be contiguous, protective, lubricious, and self-replenishing.
At elevated temperatures, added Al will preferentially oxidize and rapidly form a stable, adherent alumina scale.
An alumina-containing surface layer will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact and friction.
Al oxidation kinetics will be slower at lower temperatures.
At lower temperatures, optimized Al content or a catalytic addition will produce a nascent lubricious oxide sufficient to reduce friction.
The oxide layer will be continuously regenerated during sliding.
Continuous regeneration of the oxide layer will mitigate wear across the entire test regime.
The integral oxide layer will resist high-temperature oxidation.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has higher friction and wear because it lacks a stable protective tribolayer at both low and high temperatures.
Comparative ball-on-disk testing of baseline and Al-modified specimens can evaluate the hypothesis using COF, wear volume, and tribolayer characterization.
Absence of a statistically significant COF and wear reduction across the full range, or absence of a continuous self-healing alpha-Al2O3 layer, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The requested intervention is presented as approximately 3 wt% Al addition, but an unspecified catalytic-element addition is also proposed, making the intervention no longer strictly single or compositionally defined.

The mediator is stated as a continuous, self-replenishing alpha-Al2O3 layer across the regime, whereas the lower-temperature mechanism describes only a nascent oxide and the uncertainty field questions whether effective low-temperature alumina formation occurs.
